name: UpperTheory.V.Tower.lenDual
source: ∀ (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (M : Type) [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ_[l] M], Module.length ℤ_[l] (M →ₗ[ℤ_[l]] QZ l) = Module.length ℤ_[l] M := by
⟨fun f g => LinearMap.ext fun x => by rw [Subsingleton.elim x 0, map_zero, map_zero]⟩
have e1 := Module.length_eq_add_of_exact N.subtype N.mkQ N.injective_subtype
have e2 := Module.length_eq_add_of_exact (LinearMap.lcomp ℤ_[l] (QZ l) N.mkQ)
((dualKer l M' M' (LinearMap.id)).2 N) (exact_dual l N)
rw [e1, e2, ih, Module.length_eq_one (R := ℤ_[l]) (M := M' ⧸ N),
Module.length_eq_one (R := ℤ_[l]) (M := (M' ⧸ N) →ₗ[ℤ_[l]] QZ l), add_comm]
· have h1 : Module.length ℤ_[l] M = ⊤ := by
show: For every prime ℓ and every ℤℓ-module M, the ℤℓ-length of Hom(M,ℚℓ/ℤℓ) equals that of M, with infinity admitted.
strategy: Use exactness and preservation of simple modules along a composition series, then deal with infinite length by the annihilator inequality.

steps.claim: Write D(A) = Homℤℓ(A,ℚℓ/ℤℓ). For finite length, short exact sequences with simple quotient give length(D(M)) = length(M) by induction. For infinite length, length(M) ≤ length(D(M)) forces both lengths to be ∞.

children.claim: For every finite-length module M, length(D(M)) = length(M). Duality carries the zero module to zero and changes each simple quotient step into an exact sequence with a simple kernel.

The zero module begins the composition-series induction. At a step N ⊆ M′ with simple quotient S, the induction hypothesis gives length(D(N)) = length(N). The original short exact sequence adds length(S) to length(N), and the dual short exact sequence adds length(D(S)) to length(D(N)). Both added lengths are one.
If M′ has only its zero element, every linear functional on it vanishes. Both M′ and D(M′) have length zero.
Every x ∈ M′ equals 0, so for any f,g ∈ D(M′) one has f(x) = f(0) = 0 = g(0) = g(x). Thus the dual also has a single element.
children.snippet:
haveI : Subsingleton (M' →ₗ[ℤ_[l]] QZ l) :=
        ⟨fun f g => LinearMap.ext fun x => by rw [Subsingleton.elim x 0, map_zero, map_zero]⟩

children.claim: The module and its dual are both zero, so both lengths are 0.
For simple S = M′/N, S and D(S) both have length one. The original sequence gives length(M′) = length(N)+1 and its dual gives length(D(M′)) = 1+length(D(N)). Induction on N proves equality for M′.
The quotient S = M′/N is simple in this induction step, so its character dual D(S) is also simple.
The inclusion N → M′ is injective, the quotient map M′ → S is surjective and its kernel is N. Length additivity in this short exact sequence gives length(M′) = length(N)+length(S).
children.snippet:
have e1 := Module.length_eq_add_of_exact N.subtype N.mkQ N.injective_subtype
        N.mkQ_surjective (LinearMap.exact_subtype_mkQ N)

children.claim: The dual sequence 0 → D(S) → D(M′) → D(N) → 0 is exact. Pullback along the quotient is injective because every quotient class has a representative in M′. Restriction to N is surjective by extension of characters, and its kernel is the pullback image. Thus length(D(M′)) = length(D(S))+length(D(N)).
children.snippet:
have e2 := Module.length_eq_add_of_exact (LinearMap.lcomp ℤ_[l] (QZ l) N.mkQ)
        (LinearMap.lcomp ℤ_[l] (QZ l) N.subtype)
        (fun f g h => by
          ext x
          exact LinearMap.congr_fun h x)
        ((dualKer l M' M' (LinearMap.id)).2 N) (exact_dual l N)

children.claim: Substitute length(S) = length(D(S)) = 1 and length(D(N)) = length(N) into the two length sums. Commuting the summands gives length(D(M′)) = length(M′).
children.snippet:
rw [e1, e2, ih, Module.length_eq_one (R := ℤ_[l]) (M := M' ⧸ N),
        Module.length_eq_one (R := ℤ_[l]) (M := (M' ⧸ N) →ₗ[ℤ_[l]] QZ l), add_comm]

children.claim: If M has infinite length, the inequality length(M) ≤ length(D(M)) places ∞ below the dual length, forcing length(D(M)) = ∞ = length(M).
children.snippet: · have h1 : Module.length ℤ_[l] M = ⊤ := by

children.claim: An ℤℓ-module has finite length exactly when its extended length differs from ∞. Thus the failure of finite length gives length(M) = ∞.
children.snippet:
· have h1 : Module.length ℤ_[l] M = ⊤ := by
      rw [← not_ne_iff, Module.length_ne_top_iff]
      exact hM

children.claim: Taking annihilators in D(M) reverses strict inclusions of submodules of M. Indeed, if A is properly contained in B, a character of M/A separates a nonzero class in B/A. Reversing chains in this way gives length(M) ≤ length(D(M)). Here length(M) = ∞, so length(D(M)) = ∞.
children.snippet:
have h2 := le_dual l M
    rw [h1, top_le_iff] at h2
    rw [h1, h2]

chapterTitle: Twisted cokernels in a cyclotomic tower
